indications_original: Xylocaine (lidocaine HCl) Injections are indicated for production                            of local or regional anesthesia by infiltration techniques such as                            percutaneous injection and intravenous regional anesthesia by peripheral                            nerve block techniques such as brachial plexus and intercostal and by                            central neural techniques such as lumbar and caudal epidural blocks,                            when the accepted procedures for these techniques as described in                            standard textbooks are observed.
contraindications_original: Lidocaine HCl is contraindicated in patients with a known history                            of hypersensitivity to local anesthetics of the amide type.
adverseReactions_original: Adverse experiences following the administration of                                    lidocaine HCl are similar in nature to those observed with other                                    amide local anesthetic agents.  These adverse                                    experiences are, in general, dose-related and may result from                                    high plasma levels caused by excessive dosage, rapid absorption                                    or inadvertent intravascular injection, or may result from a                                    hypersensitivity, idiosyncrasy or diminished tolerance on the                                    part of the patient.  Serious adverse experiences are                                    generally systemic in nature.  The following types are                                    those most commonly reported:
